testCases.name: test_case_4
testCases.input: My name is Anjali and I am studying the LLM evals course. What is the difference between model evals and application evals?
testCases.actualOutput:
Hello Anjali! It's great to see your interest in understanding the differences between model evals and application evals in the context of LLM evaluations. 

To start, model evals and application evals serve distinct purposes in evaluating language models and their applications. Model evals are specifically designed to assess the capabilities of the language models themselves. This means that when a new LLM is released, model evals are used to test and benchmark its performance, often resulting in metrics like accuracy or rankings on various leaderboards. Essentially, model evals focus on the model's inherent abilities and how well it performs on specific tasks.

On the other hand, application evals are concerned with evaluating LLM-based applications. This means that instead of looking at the model in isolation, application evals assess how well the model performs within a specific application or use case. This could involve evaluating the overall effectiveness of an application that utilizes the LLM, considering factors like user experience, functionality, and the application’s ability to meet its intended goals.

It's also important to note that the terms "model eval" and "application eval" are not official industry terms; they were created to simplify the understanding of these concepts. In practice, both types are often referred to collectively as LLM evals, but the distinction is crucial for understanding what exactly is being evaluated.

So, in summary, model evals focus on the language model itself, while application evals focus on the applications that use these models. I hope this clarifies the difference for you! If you have any more questions, feel free to ask.
